details.description: Claude Fable 5 is Anthropic's first publicly available Mythos-class model, released June 9, 2026 for long-horizon agentic work, large-scale coding, and enterprise research and analysis, with text and image input and a 1M-token context window. It shares its underlying weights with the invitation-only Claude Mythos 5, but includes safety classifiers that can decline requests involving cybersecurity, biology/chemistry, or suspected model distillation. As of September 2026, Anthropic lists Fable 5 as a legacy model and recommends migrating to Claude Fable 5.1, released three months later, for improved performance.
advantages: Completed a 50-million-line codebase migration in one day, a task Stripe said would otherwise take a team over two months, per Anthropic's launch post.
Scored highest among frontier models on Cognition's FrontierCode coding evaluation, per Anthropic's launch post.
Achieved the highest score of any model on Hebbia's Finance Benchmark, per Anthropic's launch post.
Supports adaptive (always-on) thinking at a 'high' default effort level, per Anthropic's model page.
disadvantages: Legacy model: Anthropic recommends migrating to Claude Fable 5.1, released September 1, 2026, for improved performance.
Includes safety classifiers that can decline requests involving cybersecurity, biology/chemistry, or suspected model distillation, falling back to Claude Opus 4.8, per Anthropic's launch post.
use_cases: Software engineering across entire, large codebases
Multi-hour autonomous agent workflows across many tools
Enterprise research and analysis of dense filings, charts, and diagrams
Finance and knowledge work requiring extended reasoning

notes: Catalog's deprecation_date (2027-06-08) is one day off Anthropic's own tentative retirement date of 'not sooner than June 9, 2027' on both the model-deprecations table and the Fable 5 model page (likely a timezone rounding difference); kept the catalog's value. Anthropic's current models-overview page lists Fable 5 under 'Legacy models (still available)', separate from the current lineup (Fable 5.1, Opus 5.5, Sonnet 5, Haiku 4.5).
